title: Vasubandhu
hook: Asanga's brother, who wrote a great summary of the Abhidharma, then turned to "mind only"

segments.voice: Yesterday, Asanga and the dog, and Maitreya where the dog had been. Your line was compassion opened his eyes. What hurting thing did you tend? Day nine hundred sixty-two.

Asanga had a younger brother. He was brilliant, sharp in debate, and, at first, not impressed by his older brother's new Mahayana teachings at all. In fact, the old account says, he mocked them. His name was Vasubandhu, and before he was done he would write a great handbook of Buddhist thought, and then become a voice for the very teaching he had laughed at. A clever person who changed his mind in public. Today, Vasubandhu.
screen: `ASANGA'S YOUNGER BROTHER.` → `HE MOCKED THE NEW TEACHING.` → `THEN HE CHANGED HIS MIND.`

segments.voice: First, the treasury. Vasubandhu studied the Abhidharma, the careful lists that break experience into its smallest parts: moments of mind, kinds of feeling, causes and conditions. He gathered it into verses with his own commentary, the Abhidharmakosha, the Treasury of Abhidharma. Here and there in the commentary he quietly disagrees with the school he is summarizing. Even his handbook argues. Second, the turn. The Life of Vasubandhu, an old account kept in Chinese, tells it this way. Asanga, worried for his brother, sent word that he was ill. Vasubandhu came. That night he heard a Mahayana sutra being recited, and something in it reached him. He saw that he had been wrong, and he was so ashamed of the words he had spoken against it that he wanted to cut out his own tongue. Third, the answer. Asanga told him no. The tongue that had spoken against the teaching could now speak for it. Use it differently. So Vasubandhu did. Fourth, what he wrote next. He turned to the Mahayana, and wrote short, dense verses and commentaries on how the mind shapes what it sees, the teaching called mind only, which we open tomorrow. Some later writers have wondered whether two different men named Vasubandhu lie behind all these books. Tradition remembers one. Either way, the story's lesson stays the same. He did not hide his old self. He changed his mind, and put the same sharp tongue to new work.
screen: `THE TREASURY OF ABHIDHARMA.` · `A SUTRA HEARD AT NIGHT.` · `USE THE TONGUE DIFFERENTLY.` · `ON TO MIND ONLY.` · then, large: `HE CHANGED HIS MIND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: use the tongue differently. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind something you once said against a person, a place or an idea, and later saw differently. No need to cut anything out. Asanga's answer was to use the same voice for something better. So find one fair, true thing you could say now in its favor. Say it silently, once, and notice how it sits in the mouth. Rest there. The bell holds the time.
Vasubandhu. Asanga's brother, who wrote the Treasury of Abhidharma, mocked the Mahayana, then turned to it and wrote on mind only. Today's word.
Your line: he changed his mind. Today, if you find you were wrong about something, say so out loud to one person, and let it be simple. Day nine hundred sixty-two.

howItsDone: Vasubandhu's Treasury of Abhidharma is studied in Tibetan monastic colleges and in East Asian Buddhist scholarship, and his later verse works are core texts of the Yogacara school.

fork.setup: you're Vasubandhu. you've just realized the teaching you mocked was right. what do you do?
options: say nothing and hope no one remembers.
cut out the tongue that mocked it.

fork.reveal: he wanted to cut out his tongue, but Asanga stopped him: use it differently. so he wrote for the teaching he had mocked.

notes: Conversion story paraphrased from Paramartha's Life of Vasubandhu: Asanga feigned illness; Vasubandhu heard a Mahayana sutra recited (sometimes named as the Akshayamati or Dashabhumika sutra); wished to cut out his tongue; Asanga told him to use it to praise the Mahayana. Confirm.
'Here and there in the commentary he quietly disagrees with the school he is summarizing': the Kosha's bhashya often favors Sautrantika views against Vaibhashika positions. Confirm phrasing.

'Younger brother' follows the traditional account; confirm.
